newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool seen still facing flat demand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool seen still facing flat demand.

text.p: Australian wool markets faced flat retail demand in some key markets which was not expected to pick up substantially this year, the International Wool Secretariat (IWS) said on Tuesday.
Market sentiment remained focused on the short-term, it said in its monthly market briefing.
February prices had been boosted by buying from China and elsewhere, while orders from Europe and Japan for tops and yarn had increased and demand from the U.S. was firm, it said.
Fine wool prices had improved most - in February the average 19 micron indicator was 23 percent higher than in February 1996.
But pipeline stocks were feared about to start building soon, particularly in Japan and Italy, the IWS said.
Price sensitivity in Chinese raw wool demand added to the short-term focus, it said.
Industry analysts forecast the slow but volatile rise in Australian prices to continue, the IWS said.

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics forecast an average eastern market indicator of 650 cents a kg clean in 1997/98 against a current season average so far of 588 cents, it said.

Retail expenditure on textiles and apparel in Germany fell for the fourth consecutive year in 1996, as unemployment rose to levels not seen since the 1930s and continued to affect consumer confidence, it said.
Wool clothing had another tough year in Germany in 1996, with apparel wool consumption falling an estimated 7.5 percent compared with 1995, it said.
This was partly because of consumer price sensitivity and growing popularity of more casual clothing, it said.
Many retailers stocked less wool apparel than usual in autumn 1996 because of the high volume of wool clothing sold at discount in 1995, it said.
The outlook for wool apparel remained difficult in Germany with high unemployment, slow growth in personal consumption and with retailers pessimistic about future prospects, it said.
However, retail orders of wool clothing for autumn/winter 1997 should improve after the high sellout rates in autumn/winter 1996, it said.
Wool International and private stocks were currently supplying an estimated 21 percent of demand for Australian wool, it said.
